findings.title: Vault GET endpoint returns full PAN and CVV without extra gating
findings.evidence: Responds with CardDetails containing pan and cvv, documented only as 'Fetch a card's sensitive details' with scope cards:read_vault and no description, warning, or PCI note.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the sensitivity, PCI scope, and caching restrictions in the description, and mark pan/cvv as sensitive in the schema.

findings.title: Vault POST mixes spend-limit creation with sensitive detail retrieval
findings.evidence: Summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' returns PCILimit including card.pan and card.cvv, yet the 201 response is the only place these are exposed and there is no description.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into separate operations or add a description explaining what is created, what is returned, and that PAN/CVV appear only in this response.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST has empty security with 401 response
findings.evidence: 'security': [] overrides the global auth, yet the operation documents a 401 Unauthorized response and no scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the oauth2 requirement with reimbursements:write, or explain why the endpoint is unauthenticated.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: Operation is GET with summary 'Permanently delete this resource' and a 200 response 'Get single virtual card'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and check whether a DELETE operation was intended.

findings.title: Physical card GET returns 201 instead of 200
findings.evidence: Responses declare '201': Success for the GET operation, while the list GET returns 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 for the GET operation.

findings.title: Physical card POST error response is untyped string
findings.evidence: 400 response content schema is {"type":"string"} with description 'Error', unlike other operations that use DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema and add the x-trace-id header as on other 400 responses.

findings.title: Several operations lack documented error responses
findings.location: PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}, POST /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}/suspension (no 401/404), GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual, GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual/{card_id}, PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id}, GET /developer/v1/reimbursements/{reimbursement_id}
findings.evidence: These operations define only 200 (and sometimes 400), with no 401, 403, 404 or error schema, while other operations do.
findings.suggested_fix: Add consistent 401/403/404 responses with DeveloperApiErrorResponse across all operations.

findings.title: Unsuspend uses DELETE on a sub-resource with no request body
findings.evidence: Paired POST suspension is documented as revertable, but DELETE has no description and no 404 or 409 cases for already-unsuspended cards.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description and idempotency/error behavior for both suspend and unsuspend.

findings.title: Terminate card documented as 'irreversible' but no confirmation semantics
findings.evidence: Description 'Please note that this action is irreversible.' with 204 response and no 404 or repeat-call behavior documented.
findings.suggested_fix: State the effect on linked funds and transactions, and document behavior on repeat calls.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter casing in virtual cards list
findings.evidence: Parameter 'userId' is camelCase while siblings are snake_case (user_id, entity_id, is_terminated, page_size).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id, keeping userId as a deprecated alias if needed.

findings.title: Inconsistent sort parameter naming in transactions list
findings.evidence: 'orderByAmountAsc' is camelCase while 'order_by_amount_desc' and 'order_by_date_asc' are snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to order_by_amount_asc and deprecate the camelCase name.

findings.title: Transactions sort parameters are mutually-exclusive but not enforced
findings.evidence: Description says 'setting multiple ordering parameters is unsupported', but no schema or oneOf constrains it and the 400 response does not name the case.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the error returned when multiple ordering params are set, or reject them via a documented error code.

findings.title: Dangerous-sounding filter 'requires_memo' only accepts true
findings.evidence: Description says 'This can only be set to true.' but the schema is a plain boolean, so false is accepted and has unspecified behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an enum [true] or document what false does.

findings.title: Pagination styles are inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards and reimbursements use DeveloperAPINestedPage with only 'next', while transactions use DeveloperAPICountedPage with total_count; physical cards have no page_size or start parameters at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Make pagination parameters and page objects consistent across all list endpoints, or document each list's pagination model.

findings.title: Pagination 'start' cursor described as last entity ID but ambiguous
findings.evidence: start: 'The ID of the last entity of the previous page', typed as an unconstrained string; the example next link is a placeholder 'https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/<resources>?<new_params>'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give concrete cursor semantics and a real example for next, and state whether clients should follow next or build the query.

findings.title: Physical card list lacks pagination parameters despite paginated response
findings.evidence: Operation id is 'get_physical_card_list_with_pagination' and response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource, but no start or page_size parameter is declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters, or remove the pagination claim from the operation id and response.

findings.title: Default page_size documented range inconsistent with schema
findings.evidence: Description says 'between 2 and 100' but the schema has only default 20 with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2 and maximum: 100 to the schema.

findings.title: Date-time filters on reimbursements have undefined meaning
findings.evidence: 'to_transaction_date' has description 'Data.' and 'from_date'/'to_date' are documented only as 'created'. 'Filter by underlying transaction date (after this date)' conflicts with 'from_transaction_date'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace placeholder descriptions and clarify whether bounds are inclusive and which timezone applies.

findings.title: Placeholder 'Data.' descriptions on parameters
findings.evidence: Parameter include_merchant_data on GET transaction and to_transaction_date are described only as 'Data.'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write a real description for each parameter.

findings.title: Reimbursement list is missing a user_id description and mixed filters
findings.evidence: Parameter 'user_id' has no description, while 'reimbursee_id' is used in the POST body for the same concept.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description and align the naming with reimbursee_id.

findings.title: Naming inconsistency: reimbursee_id vs user_id vs spend_allocation_id
findings.evidence: Mileage body uses 'spend_allocation_id' for a fund id, 'reimbursement' uses 'fund_id' and 'spend_limit_id', and the receipt endpoint path is singular 'reimbursement' while other paths are plural.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one name for the fund concept (fund_id) and one plural path prefix, deprecating the aliases.

findings.title: Deprecated aliases still in use in responses and filters
findings.location: Transaction schema limit_id, Reimbursement spend_limit_id, Transaction amount/currency_code
findings.evidence: Transaction limit_id is marked deprecated yet is still required; amount is deprecated type number while SingleTransaction redefines amount as string.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove deprecated fields from required lists and make the type of amount consistent between Transaction and SingleTransaction.

findings.title: Transaction amount type differs between schemas
findings.evidence: Transaction defines amount as type 'number' while SingleTransaction defines the same field as type 'string'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for the same field across schemas.

findings.title: Money amounts mix units and types across endpoints
findings.evidence: Some amounts use {amount, currency_code}, some {value, currency}, and ApiSignedAmount allows negative values while ApiReimbursementAmount requires non-negative value; the required lists also differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on one money object shape and document sign rules once.

findings.title: minor_unit_conversion_rate required but nullable in several schemas
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmount requires minor_unit_conversion_rate but marks it nullable and readOnly, and the request-side CurrencyAmountRequestBody omits it.
findings.suggested_fix: Document when it is null and make required and nullable consistent.

findings.title: Transaction split endpoint PATCH is marked destructive but lacks idempotency and error details
findings.evidence: Description says it 'create[s] or replace[s]' the split and has x-destructive: true, but there are no 400, 404, or 409 responses and no documented behavior for a retry.
findings.suggested_fix: Document error cases and retry semantics for the replace-split behavior.

findings.title: Idempotency key defined inconsistently across endpoints
findings.evidence: The vault header is optional with no retry guidance, while the receipt endpoint requires an idempotency_key body field; other POST endpoints (create physical card, mileage reimbursement) have no idempotency mechanism at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header) across all POST endpoints and document retry behavior.

findings.title: Receipt upload request body schema is inconsistent with required fields
findings.evidence: reimbursement_id is optional but description says 'If omitted, a new draft reimbursement will be created via OCR', while reimbursee_id is required even when a reimbursement_id is passed.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify when reimbursee_id is required and document the conflict if both are provided.

findings.title: Enum value mismatch between enum and description for reimbursement state
findings.evidence: Both PUSH_PAYMENT_FAILED and EXPORT_FAILED are described as 'Payment failed', and REIMBURSED and REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH are both 'Paid'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each state a distinct description.

findings.title: Transaction sk_category_id enum includes unconfirmed gaps and conflicting type
findings.evidence: Example sk_category_id is the string "40,41" while the schema type is integer; enum skips 22 with no explanation.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the example to a single integer and document the missing 22.

findings.title: Vault create returns 201 but PATCH/update endpoints use 200 unevenly
findings.evidence: Creation returns 201 on vault and 200 on physical card POST, and the vault response is PCILimit whose schema name does not match the operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 201 for all creates and name the response schema consistently.

findings.title: Tag 'transactions' duplicates 'Transaction' tag
findings.evidence: Tags include both 'Transaction' and lowercase 'transactions', and the PATCH operation carries both.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate tag and use one canonical name.

findings.title: Physical card display_name listed as required but read-only and possibly absent
findings.evidence: required includes 'display_name' and 'expiration', both readOnly, while the PATCH body allows setting display_name.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove read-only fields from required lists or clarify how they are populated for unactivated cards.
